title: DFT Scaling Behavior Chart
description: A Chart.js comparison of quadratic DFT growth against a linear algorithm from N = 8 to 1024, with a log-scale toggle and a draggable marker reading both curves.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Algorithm Analysis
Performance
chapter_title: Why the DFT Is Too Slow

educational.topic: Asymptotic growth of the direct DFT
learningObjectives: Examine operation count as a function of N
Compare quadratic and linear growth at realistic window sizes
Explain why the penalty ratio is itself N
prerequisites: The direct DFT is a double loop

controls.label: Logarithmic Y-axis
controls.purpose: Make both curves comparable across orders of magnitude

controls.label: Either curve
controls.purpose: Tooltip with exact N and operation count

assumptions: One operation per multiply-accumulate; constant factors ignored
The linear series is a hypothetical reference, not a real algorithm
limitations: The FFT is O(N log N), between these two curves; it is introduced in the next chapter rather than plotted here

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Comparative growth curves with a movable read-off marker
keyQuestions: Why does the linear curve look flat on a linear axis?
What is the ratio between the curves, and why does it grow?
commonMisconceptions: That hand-optimizing the inner loop can close an asymptotic gap
That the flat blue line means the linear series is missing or zero
assessmentOpportunities: Judge whether a 30% constant-factor speedup rescues a doubling of N
